channel.title: MIND / MATTER Daily Briefing
channel.description: New research across consciousness, quantum foundations, and neuroscience.

item.title: Effects of auditory sensory stimulation on consciousness and physiological parameters among individuals with disorders of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: Objective To systematically evaluate the effects of auditory sensory stimulation (SS) on consciousness levels and physiological parameters in patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC). Furthermore, this study aimed to explore intervention characteristics based on the frequency, intensity, time, and type (FITT) framework that may influence treatment effects and to investigate potential sources of between-study heterogeneity.

item.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
item.description: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future $e^+e^-$ colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes $e^+ e^- \to t\bar{t},\ e^+e^-\to μ^+μ^-$ and Bhabha scattering $e^+e^-\to e^+e^-$, representing the mass threshold behavior, the $Z$ pole resonance and the $s/t$-channel interplay.

item.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
item.description: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions.

item.title: Quantum Machine Learning
item.description: Quantum machine learning (QML) has emerged as a rapidly developing field at the intersection of quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and data science. As quantum hardware and algorithms continue to advance, there is a growing need for a rigorous and accessible text that explains how quantum principles can be used to design, analyze, and implement machine learning models.

item.title: Decoding sequence auditory expectations for clinical diagnostic and prognostic assessment of prolonged disorders of consciousness
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Electroencephalogram (EEG) features are important objective markers for diagnostic and prognostic evaluation of prolonged disorders of consciousness (DOC). However, task-based EEG paradigms are limited by mismatches between task demands and patients' residual awareness, as well as the limited individual assessment capacity of machine-learning-based detection frameworks.

item.title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature
item.description: Abstract Fragmentation is common in interdisciplinary fields with diverse methods and theoretical commitments. Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve.

item.title: The Association Between Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Postoperative Delirium: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
item.description: Background: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious complication following surgery, particularly in high-risk patients such as those with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The relationship between COPD and the development of POD remains unclear, with existing studies providing inconsistent findings.

item.title: Measurement-informed dynamical decoupling for fidelity preservation on large-scale quantum processors
item.description: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a key technique for suppressing decoherence and preserving the performance of quantum algorithms. We introduce a measurement-based DD (MDD) protocol that determines control unitary gates from partial measurements of noisy subsystems, with measurement overhead scaling linearly with the number of subsystems.

item.title: Digital engineering for quantum communication networks: A systematic review of models, simulators, and testbeds
item.description: Research on quantum communication networks has grown rapidly in recent years, driven by progress in quantum devices, simulators, and experimental testbeds. As these systems become more complex, there is increasing interest in digital methods that can support analysis, prediction, and performance assessment without relying exclusively on physical experimentation.

item.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
item.description: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target.

item.title: Quantum Fourier integration of decay rates at next-to-leading order
item.description: We discuss the use of quantum neural networks (QNNs) as a tool for integrating decay rates at next-to-leading order (NLO) in perturbation theory. Data-encoding quantum circuits admit a truncated Fourier-series representation, enabling a trained QNN to approximate a target integrand and provide the coefficients subsequently integrated with Quantum Fourier Iterative Amplitude Estimation (QFIAE).

item.title: Accelerating Quantum-Classical Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo with Shadow-Trained Neural Quantum States
item.description: Quantum-classical auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) uses a trial state prepared on a quantum computer to improve the accuracy of the classical AFQMC algorithm. State-of-the-art QC-AFQMC represents this state with matchgate shadows, so every trial-walker overlap and local energy must be averaged over many snapshots, making this classical computation a bottleneck.

item.title: Approaching quantum limits in sub-Rayleigh resolution using phase modulation optimization
item.description: Spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) has made significant progress in incoherent optical imaging and has been implemented through various experimental approaches. Holography-based SPADE is widely used in proof-of-principle experiments because of its low cost, stable optical arrangement, and ease of implementation.

item.title: Higher-order topological quantum battery
item.description: A quantum battery is a next-generation energy-storage device that exploits genuinely quantum properties such as superposition and coherence. We propose a second-order topological quantum battery coupled to a photonic crystal described by the breathing-Kagome model, where optical loss is present on all lattice sites while nonlinear gains are introduced selectively at the output sites.

item.title: Dithered Belief Propagation for Real-Time Quantum Memory Decoding
item.description: We introduce dithered belief-propagation decoding for circuit-level quantum memory to mitigate the oscillations and trapping behavior that limit standard belief-propagation (BP) decoders for qLDPC codes. Our approach combines a quantum-adapted sign-flip mechanism with chained randomized prior perturbation.

item.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life
item.description: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes. A previous digital-life framework distinguishes online (busy) and offline (idle) channels, but leaves open whether these are separate programs or phases of a common process and how their operations should be ordered.
